name: application-column-visibility-menu
title: Column Visibility Menu
description: "Columns" trigger button that opens a checklist of toggleable table columns with drag handles for reordering and a locked row for required columns.
useWhen: Pairing with a data table so users can show, hide, and reorder columns to fit their workflow.
You need to protect one or more columns (e.g. Status, ID) from being hidden while still letting users reorder or hide the rest.
The table has enough columns that a fixed layout no longer fits every user's needs.
avoidWhen: The table has a small, fixed set of columns that never needs customization — the extra control adds clutter without value.
You need column width resizing rather than visibility/order — that's a separate concern from this menu.
responsiveBehavior: The panel is a fixed-width dropdown anchored to its trigger; on narrow viewports it may need to switch to a full-width sheet rather than an anchored popover.
accessibility: The trigger carries aria-haspopup and aria-expanded reflecting open state; the panel closes on Escape or an outside click.
Each column row is a real <label>/<input type="checkbox"> pair, not a custom-styled div, so it's natively operable and announced correctly.
Required columns render a real disabled checkbox plus a visible "Required" label, not just a muted color, so the restriction is understandable without relying on color alone.
Drag handles are decorative (aria-hidden); reordering should also be exposed via a non-drag interaction (e.g. keyboard move up/down) in a full implementation for parity.

variants.title: Column Visibility Menu
variants.description: An open "Columns" panel with Name, Email, and Role checked, Company unchecked, and a locked, disabled Status row marked Required, plus a Reset to default action.
accessibility: The required column's lock state is conveyed by both a disabled checkbox and visible text, not styling alone.

variants.title: Column Visibility Menu (Dark)
variants.description: The same column checklist and required-row lock adapted for dark surfaces.
accessibility: Checkbox and label contrast remain distinguishable at dark-surface contrast, including the muted required row.
